_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.298 / rev27v-followup-292 preserves the valve during normal sealed primitive transitions, correcting the measured 10–12 mmHg standalone pressure loss between inflation and deflation. STOP and fault paths retain their vent/pump-off behavior. Deflation handoff uses active gains and achievable output, with anti-windup based on delivered valve duty. GUI settling now counts from inflation completion.

Simulator recordings retain physical units, exact Arduino sequence delivery, active PID startup/error, and NI failed-read/interval diagnostics. Both layout audits and smoke tests passed. Protected flash/restore and ten-minute seed-213 soaks passed: Default 6/6 with 100.00% Arduino delivery; Valinor 8/8 hard gates with 100.00% delivery. Six matched GUI/standalone trials and three final GUI trials completed with zero NI sample gaps. Final GUI settling was 2.89–2.95 s; standalone about 2.53 s.

Measured limitations remain: a shared startup duty valley, MAP disagreement with the independent cuff oscillogram, pulse preservation below 20 mmHg, and cross-cuff SysID qualification. The original 270-trial wrist/syringe experiment preserves 85 completed trials; the remaining 185 retain their original indices/settings. A SysID threshold candidate was withheld after increasing historical rejections.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
